bullets.title: Market structure: Nasdaq 100 in correction; S&P breadth positive as equal-weight leads
bullets.body: The Nasdaq 100 fell ~1.6% on the session and entered correction territory (down 10%+ from June ATH), with the SOX in a 25.7% drawdown and four consecutive sessions of weakness. Meanwhile equal-weight S&P 500 outperformed cap-weighted by ~90 bps and hit new ATHs, with breadth solidly positive — reflecting violent rotation rather than broad market collapse. Healthcare, staples, software, regional banks, payments, cruise lines, and airlines outperformed; semis, energy, and AI-adjacent names lagged.

bullets.title: AI/momentum selloff accelerating: Goldman's high-beta momentum basket on pace for worst monthly performance in history
bullets.body: Goldman's high-beta momentum basket is tracking for its worst monthly decline on record, worse than 2000 and 2009. GS TMT Momentum Pair (leaders vs laggards) is down 40%+ in July. JPM TMT specialist cited weak earnings prints, circular financing concerns, anxiety over CSP capex cuts, and elevated positioning as the four drivers. H/F de-grossing reached largest pace since Sep 2025; Global Info Tech saw largest long selling in past two sessions since January 2021.

bullets.title: FOMC tomorrow: JPM/22V expect hawkish hold with ~30% hike probability; market pricing ~35-40%
bullets.body: JPM expects the Fed to hold with at least two hawkish dissents (Hammack, Logan) and assigns 50% probability to a hawkish hold (SPX flat to -50 bps), 20% to a 25 bp hike (SPX -1.5% to -2%, NDX amplified 2-4x), and 28% to a dovish hold (SPX +50-100 bps). Citadel Securities separately argued for a hike. BofA notes a July hike would be unprecedented — the Fed has not hiked with less than 60% market-priced odds since 1994. FOMC press conference with Chair Warsh at 2:30 pm ET Wednesday.

bullets.title: Oil plunges 5%+ to below $80/bbl on US-Iran détente signals; Hormuz flow physically halted
bullets.body: Brent crude fell more than 5% to below $84/bbl and WTI dropped below $80 — a third consecutive day of declines — on reports mediators believe the US and Iran are close to resurrecting a failed MoU deal. Paradoxically, zero tankers are transiting the Strait of Hormuz in either direction per physical flow data, with oil algo-selling dominant. Saudi Aramco also shut its 400k bpd Jazan refinery after a Red Sea attack. JPMorgan's global inflation monitor notes its $83/bbl Brent baseline; a Hormuz/Red Sea disruption scenario would push inflation to ~4% annualized.

bullets.title: Iran-US Hormuz standoff: Iran rejects Omani route, threatens to block strait for entities seizing frozen assets
bullets.body: Iran's deputy FM denied seeking US talks in the past 16-17 days, rejected the Omani-proposed Hormuz route, and threatened to bar strait access for any country or company receiving Iranian frozen assets. Iran also claimed the US sent messages via Oman assuring no attack. Diplomatic impasse remains; GOP advancing Graham sanctions bill.

bullets.title: Consumer confidence miss and labor market softening add to macro headwinds
bullets.body: July Consumer Confidence came in at 90.8 vs 92.4 consensus, declining for a third straight month with the present situations index at multi-year lows. ADP private payrolls averaged 15k/week in the four weeks ending July 11, the fifth consecutive weekly slowdown, down from 35,750/week in early May. Home prices beat in May, but the Conference Board survey flagged the weakest 'present situation' labor reading in 5+ years.

bullets.title: 7-year Treasury auction weak on domestic side; 30-year TIPS real yield hits record high
bullets.body: The 7-year note auction cleared at 4.473% (up 21 bps from prior), with direct bidder participation collapsing from 29.7% to 16.9% while indirect (foreign) buyers stepped up to 70.1% from 57.6%. Separately, 30-year TIPS real yield hit an all-time record high. JPM recommends 5s/30s flatteners as hawkish repricing continues; expects August refunding to hold coupon sizes steady with coupon increases beginning February 2027.

bullets.title: NVDA/AMD circular financing concerns weigh on semis; UBS pushes back, projects $900B NVDA FCF through 2028
bullets.body: The semis correction has been amplified by perceived circular financing (NVDA backing $50B leases for HUT Texas site; AMD partnering with CORZ on 2.5GW capacity), open-weight model proliferation, memory cycle sustainability questions, and crowded positioning. UBS pushes back, arguing NVDA will generate ~$900B FCF through CYE2028 with MU ~$450B and AMD ~$90B, and that hyperscaler FCF turns only mildly negative in C2027 (~$60B) before memory normalization in late C2027/mid-C2028 improves the picture. Mag 7 positioning at 1-year lows (3rd percentile) ahead of megacap earnings.

bullets.title: China mass-producing domestic DUV lithography; Korean markets hit circuit breakers on chip rout
bullets.body: China has begun mass production of domestic immersion DUV lithography tools (SMEE reportedly shipping to SMIC, CXMT, YMTC since May 2025), raising long-term equipment self-sufficiency concerns — though BofA and multiple analysts argue it is still years from threatening ASML's position. South Korea's KOSPI volatility hit an all-time high (exceeding 1997 and 2020 extremes), with memory-chip stocks now comprising over 50% of the index. Asian chip stocks posted their worst single day since Liberation Day.

bullets.title: Apple hits $5T market cap (2nd ever after NVDA); launches Klarna-powered device leasing program
bullets.body: Apple briefly surpassed $5 trillion in market cap, only the second company to do so after Nvidia. Simultaneously, Apple launched 'Apple Upgrade,' a Klarna-powered 0%-interest device leasing program (iPhone from $17.99/mo, MacBook Air from $24.99/mo, iPad from $11.99/mo), replacing the prior upgrade/payments programs. Analysts note this removes the need for price cuts while expanding ecosystem access; HomePad smart home device also reportedly on track for October launch.

bullets.title: Global inflation: June CPI slows to 3.3% YoY on energy; baseline 2.7% for 2H but risks skewed higher
bullets.body: JPMorgan's global inflation monitor shows June CPI ex-China/Turkey fell 0.1% MoM, decelerating to 3.3% YoY and 3.0% on a 3-month annualized basis. The 2H26 baseline assumes $83/bbl Brent and headline at ~2.7% annualized; a Hormuz/Red Sea disruption scenario lifts inflation to ~4%. US core goods momentum slid to -0.7% 3m annualized; global core services edging down. BIS economists separately warned the AI boom is distorting economic signals and increasing central bank miscalibration risk.

bullets.title: Broad AI capex ROI skepticism grows; open-weight models seen pressuring frontier providers
bullets.body: Multiple sources — 22V, FactSet evening recap, and GS TMT — confirm persistent investor concern about AI capex sustainability and ROI on hyperscaler spend. The narrative is reinforced by Nasdaq 100 entering correction. Open-weight models and China competition are cited as incremental headwinds to frontier providers. 22V notes 74% of investors still expect next 10% momentum move to be higher, and AI services/application-layer companies are seen as potential beneficiaries as intelligence commoditizes.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler credit spreads at record: cost to insure AI hyperscaler default hits new highs
bullets.body: The cost of insuring against default by AI hyperscalers has hit record levels per one source, and MS Credit notes IBOXIG TRS NAV basis near record compression with client positioning at record net longs. MS credit desk favors shorting IBOXIG TRS on basis re-widening and prefers ratio payer spreads as low-premium widening expressions.

bullets.title: HF leverage unwind largest since Sep 2025; all three HF styles down >1% same day for first time since COVID
bullets.body: Fundamental L/S -1.3%, Systematic L/S -1.0%, Multi-Strats -1.7% as of noon on July 28 — first time all three down >1% simultaneously since March 2020. Gross leverage fell 13.5 pts since end of May, reversing ~45% of YTD build. Memory names saw largest net selling on a 2-day basis since the AI trade first gained popularity. Mag7 net exposure at 3rd percentile vs 1-year history.

bullets.title: OPEC+ expected to pause output hikes after September through year-end 2026
bullets.body: Multiple sources report OPEC+ delegates expect the cartel to hold 2026 output steady after the September increase, pausing through the remainder of the year. This comes as Brent crude is already down 5%+ on diplomatic Iran headlines.

bullets.title: Treasury Secretary Bessent touts strong economy; core inflation at 2.6%, record investment inflows
bullets.body: Treasury Secretary Bessent stated the underlying economy is very strong, consumer remains resilient, lower-income workers are seeing larger wage gains, core inflation has eased to 2.6%, and record investment is flowing into the US. He described current conditions as a 'manufacturing renaissance.'

bullets.title: Rotation playbook: Financials, staples, healthcare, software outperform; semis/servers/energy lag
bullets.body: The S&P 500 Financials Index rose 1.2% with Cards/Payments +2.3% and Regional Banks +1.7%. Equal-weight S&P hit new ATHs while cap-weighted lagged. Consumer staples (XLP +2%), healthcare, media (+1.7% Communications Services), and software (IGV volume 2x+ recent trend) led rotational inflows. Energy, Medicaid MCOs, and semiconductor names lagged. Dow Jones +1.03% vs Nasdaq -0.22%.

bullets.title: Meta + BlackRock announce $14B El Paso data center joint venture
bullets.body: Meta and BlackRock announced a $14 billion partnership to develop and operate a data center in El Paso focused on AI infrastructure, representing one of the largest single data center investments disclosed this cycle.

bullets.title: FOMC dovish-hold scenario: Warsh faces board opposition; rate hike at July unprecedented per BofA
bullets.body: Multiple sources note Chair Warsh wants to do 'the right thing' but faces opposition among the 12 FOMC voters. BofA notes the Fed has not hiked since 1994 when less than 60% market odds were priced, suggesting a July hike is historically unprecedented. One macro analyst (MacDonell) argues raising rates as a 'credibility stunt' is weak policy logic — real Fed credibility comes from avoiding frequent direction reversals.

bullets.title: Seagate massive beat-and-raise on AI data center demand; Q1 guide ~25% above Street
bullets.body: STX delivered fiscal Q4 revenue of $3.63B (+48% YoY, beat $3.50B est.) with EPS of $5.71 (+121% YoY, beat $5.10 est.), gross margins 52.7% (+1,480 bps YoY), and FCF $1.1B. F1Q27 guidance of $4.1B revenue and $7.30 EPS was ~25% above Street expectations of $3.78B/$5.85, with ~90% of shipments going to data center customers. Stock +7.3% after hours.
